q: 200 people upload a 50 MB video at the same time, and the bytes go through your API (in from the phone, out to storage). How much data do your API servers carry?
options: 10 GB
0.2 MB
20 GB
50 MB
why: 200 x 50 MB in, plus the same out again, is 20 GB. With signed links the API only sees the small request for the link, and the video goes straight to storage.

q: The API builds the upload key from the caller's input: body.key || "uploads/" + user.id + "/" + body.fileId. User 42 sends key "uploads/7/passport.jpg". What can happen?
options: Nothing, the link is only for user 42
Storage refuses because the user id is wrong
User 42 can replace user 7's file, because a same-key upload replaces the old object
The upload goes into a new version automatically
why: The server must pick the key itself. S3 replaces an existing object when a new file is uploaded to the same key (unless versioning keeps the old one).

q: Someone takes a signed upload link and changes the key in the path. Why does storage refuse it?
options: The signature was worked out from the key, so the signature storage works out now is different
The link can only be used once
Storage asks your API every time
The new key is too long
why: Storage holds the same secret and works out the signature again from the key, the time, the method and the signed headers. Any change gives another signature.

q: A 100 GiB file with 5 MiB parts would be 20,480 parts. What is true?
options: That is fine, there is no limit on parts
That is above the limit of 10,000 parts, so use bigger parts, such as 11 MiB
Parts must be exactly 5 GiB
The file is too big for S3
why: One multipart upload has at most 10,000 parts. 100 GiB / 10,000 is about 10.2 MiB, so 11 MiB parts (9,310 of them) work. The file size is far below the 48.8 TiB limit.

q: The phone says the upload is done. What should turn the row from pending to ready?
options: The phone's message, because it knows best
A timer of 5 minutes
The storage event, after a check that the size and type match
The next time the user opens the app
why: Storage knows what really arrived. The row stays pending until the event (or your own check) confirms it. Old pending rows are marked expired by a cleanup job.

q: What does the AWS documentation say about a presigned URL?
options: It can be used once, and then it is gone
It works for anyone who holds it, and can be used more than once until it expires
It only works from the IP address of the person who asked for it
It never expires
why: The docs call presigned URLs bearer tokens. Whoever holds one can use it, more than once, until it expires. Keep the lifetime to minutes.
